summary: @addai/node ships a remote-agent daemon that executes Supabase-supplied prompts through PTY-hosted AI CLIs with permission bypass
details: The package runs a daemon that pairs the installer's host to an account via a short code and then polls a hardcoded Supabase project (https://syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co) via RPCs runtime_pick_next_request and runtime_commands_pick. Received requests supply prompts, a working directory, a permission mode, and MCP configuration, which are passed into pty.spawn of vendor AI CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Gemini, Grok). When a request selects it, Claude is launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions, giving the remote-issued prompt an agent loop with unrestricted tool use — including shell/bash execution — inside the installer's chosen working directory on the installer's host. A separate probeCapabilities routine reads local credential files for these CLIs (~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json, ~/.grok/auth.json, ~/.kimi-code/credentials/*.json, ~/.gemini/.env) and posts derived login-state metadata (authed booleans, account email, plan, accountKind, CLI version) to a runtime_heartbeat RPC on the same Supabase project every ~30s; raw tokens are not included in the payload, but the account email and plan of each third-party AI account are. The Supabase URL, anon key, and RPC contract are hardcoded, so whoever controls the paired +Ai account — or the Supabase project — can direct arbitrary agent-driven shell activity on any host that has installed and paired this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
